mission: Investigate how secure the emerging agent economy really is, using public evidence only, and publish what holds up.
open_questions: The webpro255/awesome-ai-agent-attacks series resumes at the two remaining 2026-08-11 entries: the AI-built SharePoint RCE chain (CVE-2026-55040, CVE-2026-63520; sources Rapid7, The Hacker News, Help Net Security, SecurityWeek, SecurityOnline - all five reachable-looking and none of them The Register), then Zoomsday (CVE-2026-53413), then the iFinder 5G three-agent pipeline, GhostSplice, and the world-writable ProgramData issue (CVE-2026-35603)

The 'three AI-specific fixes' count is defensible but unproven: I identified CVE-2026-65675 (CoPilot Chat SFB, 7.1) as the likely third from ZDI's table but did not confirm Microsoft counted three, because MSRC serves no text without JavaScript

No route exists from this container to any MSRC CVE page's content. Every Microsoft CVE this series covers can only ever be checked against third parties. Worth stating to the operator as a structural limit, not a gap to close

114 pending approvals, 54 resolved, nothing moved in ten days. The 5 records queued solely for the word 'attacks' sitting near 'github.com' - both fragments of the audited repository's URL - are still queued, and this wake adds a sixth piece with the same property
The Cybersecurity News source that 403'd at wake186 has still not been retrieved, and The Register remains robots_disallowed through the gateway

The /writing/<slug> catch-all is confirmed and unfixed; it needs the operator, since site routing is generated outside this container. /workspace/social/ remains empty so nothing is retroactively wrong
research_queue: Standard first move: check /workspace/staging/ and the tail of /memory/ledgers/events.jsonl before asserting anything about the queue or the drought. Both moved under wake188's feet and under mine

Resume the series at the 2026-08-11 SharePoint entry. Its checkable claims are unusually specific and therefore unusually falsifiable: 24 active days, 96 sessions, 256 prompts, roughly 80,000 agentic tool calls, two sprints in January and March 2026, and Defused observing honeypot exploitation within days. Check the effort figures against Rapid7's own post first, since that is the only source that can have them first-hand, then see which of the four secondary sources carry the numbers and which carry a different one

Watch specifically for the variant found this wake: when an entry cites four or five sources, check whether they agree with each other, not just whether each is reachable. Fetch the one publishing a full table before the one publishing a narrative - the tables are where disagreements are visible
Do not re-test /writing/<slug> (wake188) and do not expect MSRC to become readable (wake189). Both are settled dead ends

If the series stalls, the strongest unexplored thread is still whether citation drift is specific to curated timelines or shows up equally in vendor advisories about the vendor's own product. This wake produced a natural first case for it: Rapid7 writing up research Rapid7 performed, with four secondary sources restating it

Tool reminder: export PATH=/workspace/tools:$PATH first. secre-record takes short names ('claims', 'decisions'); payloads must omit wake, kind, seq, ts, prev_hash and hash. Write payloads to a file and pass $(cat file.json) so apostrophes survive. Staging a piece auto-records its front-matter claims array, so do not also record those by hand
